about: Other ways drafters write the problems the lint checks. mscd_lint.py runs each pattern as a direct finding; its self-test runs every example (which must be caught) and look-alike (which must not be). Add a variant here, with an example, rather than in the code. A lookalike shows only that this one check must not fire on it; it may break another rule (the self-test checks 1 check at a time). Correct text lives in references/look-alikes.md.

checks.pattern: \b(?:IN NO EVENT|AT NO TIME|UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES?|IN NO CASE|ON NO ACCOUNT|IN NO INSTANCE)\s*,?\s+(?:SHALL|WILL)\b
checks.message: In no event shall (or will) in conspicuous text: shall with a negative subject reads as absence of duty, not prohibition (MSCD 3.324; house rule 8). For a cap on liability, state the policy: ACME'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY WILL NOT EXCEED ...; for a prohibition on a party, NEITHER PARTY MAY ...
examples: IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED $500,000.
UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES WILL SUPPLIER SUBCONTRACT THE SERVICES.
lookalikes: IN NO EVENT IS LICENSOR LIABLE FOR INDIRECT DAMAGES.
Acme shall not disclose the Terms at any time.

checks.message: Covenants (or agrees, undertakes) piled onto represents or warrants makes no sense: a statement of fact isn't an obligation (MSCD 3.414). Delete the extra verb; if the party must also do something, state that separately with shall (MSCD 3.451). For the rest, on Blake's draft write states; on the other side's draft keep represents and warrants (house rule 10).
examples: Seller represents, warrants, and covenants to Buyer that Seller has good title to the Shares.
Licensor represents, warrants and covenants that the Software contains no Malicious Code.
Licensee covenants and warrants that it will not reverse engineer the Software.
Seller represents and warrants and agrees that the Equipment is free of any Lien.
lookalikes: Seller states that the Equipment is free of any Lien.
Seller acknowledges that Buyer would not have entered into this agreement without the covenants in the section titled "Noncompetition."
Licensee shall comply with each covenant in the section titled "Use Restrictions."

checks.message: A promise after represents, warrants or states (represents and warrants that it will perform ...) is an obligation dressed as a statement of fact: move it to language of obligation (Contractor shall perform ...). This applies on either side's draft (MSCD 3.451; 13.948).
examples: Contractor represents and warrants that it will perform the Services in accordance with the Specifications.
Acme warrants that it shall perform routine maintenance on the Equipment.
Supplier represents that it will not use any Subcontractor without Customer's consent.
lookalikes: Seller states that the Equipment is free of any Lien.
Contractor shall perform the Services in accordance with the Specifications.
Seller states that the Products will be free from defects for 12 months after delivery.

checks.message: Keep represents (or warrants) on the other side's draft and suggest the remedies-neutral sentence in a comment; on Blake's draft write states (MSCD 3.457; 13.937; house rule 10). A warranty of goods in a sale of goods keeps warrants (MSCD 3.415; 3.453).

checks.message: Keep this lead-in on the other side's draft and suggest the remedies-neutral sentence in a comment; on Blake's draft write [Party] states that the following facts are accurate: (MSCD 3.457; 3.458; house rule 10).

checks.message: Passive statement of fact (It is represented and warranted by Seller that ...): name the party as subject. On Blake's draft write Seller states that ...; on the other side's draft, Seller represents and warrants that ... (house rule 1; MSCD 3.27; 3.457; house rule 10).
examples: It is represented and warranted by Seller that no Proceeding is pending against Seller.
It is hereby warranted to Buyer that the Units are new.

checks.message: Confirms (or asserts) to introduce a statement of fact: write states (MSCD 3.457).
examples: Seller confirms to Buyer that the Financial Statements fairly present Company's financial condition.
Licensee asserts that it owns the Licensee Data.

checks.message: Hereby with a statement of fact: delete hereby; it belongs only in language of performance (MSCD 3.412; 3.53).
examples: Licensor hereby represents and warrants to Licensee that the Software does not infringe any patent.

lookalikes: Seller hereby sells the Assets to Buyer for the Purchase Price.

Licensor makes no representation or warranty about the Third-Party Components.

State a period for acting: Customer shall pay each invoice no later than 30 days after receiving it; for discretion, say how long it lasts (MSCD 10.57).

checks.message: Agrees that (or undertakes that, covenants that) in front of shall, will, may or must is throat-clearing: delete it and state the provision directly (Contractor shall obtain ...; Licensee may sublicense ...) (MSCD 3.45; 3.27). Where will states a duty, write shall (MSCD 3.111).

checks.message: Agrees not to (or undertakes not to, covenants not to) for a prohibition: write shall not (Employee shall not solicit ...) (MSCD 3.321).
examples: Employee agrees not to solicit any customer of Company during the Restricted Period.

checks.message: Agrees to (split by with [party] or a comma phrase) for an obligation: write shall (Tenant shall pay ...) (MSCD 3.125).
examples: Tenant agrees with Landlord to pay the Rent on the 1st day of each month.
Buyer agrees, at its own expense, to obtain each consent that the Assumed Contracts require.
lookalikes: Tenant shall pay the Rent on the 1st day of each month.
The parties agree with each other as follows:

checks.message: Agrees to: for an obligation write shall (MSCD 3.125). If the act takes effect on signing (a release, assignment, grant or waiver), use language of performance: HEREBY RELEASES (MSCD 3.59).
examples: EMPLOYEE AGREES TO RELEASE COMPANY FROM ALL CLAIMS ARISING OUT OF EMPLOYEE'S EMPLOYMENT.
LICENSEE AGREES NOT TO REVERSE ENGINEER THE SOFTWARE.

checks.message: Promises to: write shall (Borrower shall pay ...); MSCD 3.128 says this applies even in a promissory note. Keep promises to pay to the order of in a negotiable note: the order language makes it negotiable under UCC 3-104(a), so treat it as wording the law requires and flag it rather than change it.
examples: Borrower promises to pay Lender the principal amount of $500,000, with interest at the Note Rate.
Each Guarantor promises to reimburse Lender for each cost of collection.
lookalikes: FOR VALUE RECEIVED, Borrower promises to pay to the order of Lender the principal amount of $500,000.
In consideration of the mutual promises to perform in this agreement, the parties agree as follows:
Each Member shall deliver a written promise to repay any advance.

checks.message: Commits to, is committed to, pledges to, binds itself to and is bound to: for an obligation, write shall (Investor shall fund ...) (MSCD 3.129).
examples: Consultant commits to providing the Services at the rates in Schedule A.
Manufacturer is committed to supplying all of Distributor's requirements for the Products during the Term.

checks.message: Is obligated to (or is obliged to) for a duty: write shall (Supplier shall replace ...) (MSCD 3.130). It is long-winded and could suggest the duty arises elsewhere.
examples: Supplier is obligated to replace each defective Unit at Supplier's cost.
Contractor is obliged to remedy each Defect that appears during the Defects Liability Period.
lookalikes: Supplier is not obligated to replace any Unit that Customer damages.
Seller shall pay each amount that Seller is obligated to pay under the section titled "Indemnification."

checks.message: Has a duty to (or has an obligation to, is under an obligation to) in contract text: write shall (Seller shall deliver ...) (MSCD 3.131; 3.130).
examples: Seller has an obligation to deliver the Units to Buyer's warehouse.
Each party is under a duty to mitigate its Losses.
The parties have a duty to cooperate in preparing the Closing Statement.
lookalikes: Seller has no obligation to repair any Unit that Buyer damages.
If Seller has an obligation to withhold Taxes under applicable law, Seller may withhold them.
Seller shall deliver the Units to Buyer's warehouse.

checks.message: Is required to for a duty this agreement imposes on a party: write shall (Buyer shall deliver ...) (MSCD 3.89). Like is obligated to (MSCD 3.130), it is wordy and may suggest the duty arises elsewhere, and it is passive (house rule 1). Keep is not required to (house rule 1's fixed exception); for a nonparty, use must (MSCD 3.166).
examples: Buyer is required to deliver the Deposit to the Escrow Agent no later than 2 Business Days after the date of this agreement.
The parties are required to meet each Quarter to review the Forecast.
lookalikes: Acme is not required to repair the Equipment after the Warranty Period ends.
If Seller is required to disclose Confidential Information by applicable law, Seller shall notify Buyer.
Buyer shall pay each amount that Buyer is required to pay under the section titled "Fees."

checks.message: Passive may not (This agreement may not be assigned ...): it hides who is prohibited, and may not can also mean might not (MSCD 3.307; house rule 1). Name the party: Neither party may assign this agreement ...; Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold its consent. For what it takes to amend or waive, state a condition: An amendment to this agreement will not be effective unless both parties sign it (MSCD 3.546; 3.369).
examples: This agreement may not be assigned by either party without the other party's consent.
This agreement may not be amended except in a writing that both parties sign.
Confidential Information may not be used for any purpose other than the Purpose.
Landlord's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
lookalikes: Each party acknowledges that monetary damages may not be a sufficient remedy for a breach of this section.
Licensee acknowledges that the Software may not be suited to every use.
Neither party may assign this agreement without the other party's consent.

checks.message: May never (or may in no event, may at no time) for a prohibition: write shall not (Licensee shall not use ...) (MSCD 3.307). If the prohibition must outlast this agreement, say so (MSCD 3.319).
examples: Licensee may never use the Licensed Marks as part of a corporate name.
Buyer may in no event resell the Units to a Competitor.
Tenant may at no time store Hazardous Materials on the Premises.
lookalikes: Licensee may at any time terminate this agreement by notifying Licensor.
Licensee shall not use the Licensed Marks as part of a corporate name.

checks.message: Cannot for a prohibition: write shall not (Customer shall not modify ...) (MSCD 3.321). Keep cannot only for inability (If Seller cannot deliver clear title, ...).
examples: Customer cannot modify the Equipment without Supplier's consent.
Each party cannot disclose the terms of this agreement to anyone other than its Representatives.
lookalikes: If Seller cannot deliver clear title, Buyer may terminate this agreement.
Licensee acknowledges that Licensor cannot guarantee that the Software will operate without interruption.
Supplier shall give Customer a credit for each Unit that Supplier cannot deliver.

checks.message: Is prohibited from (or is forbidden to): write shall not (Contractor shall not remove ...) (MSCD 3.305); the passive also hides who imposes the prohibition (house rule 1).
examples: Contractor is prohibited from removing from the Site any equipment that Owner owns.
Licensee is expressly prohibited from sublicensing the Software.
Licensee is strictly prohibited from reverse engineering the Software.
Tenant is forbidden to sublet the Premises.
lookalikes: If Seller is prohibited from disclosing the information by applicable law, Seller shall notify Buyer.

checks.message: Is not permitted to (or is not allowed to, is not authorized to) for a prohibition: write shall not (Lessee shall not move ...) (MSCD 3.305; 3.206).
examples: Lessee is not permitted to move the Equipment from the Premises without Lessor's consent.
Distributor is not allowed to sell the Products outside the Territory.
lookalikes: Mancini is not entitled to serve on Widgetco's board of directors.

checks.message: May not for a prohibition with an affirmative subject: write shall not (MSCD 3.307). If the sentence is a no-reliance clause, state it as a declaration: CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT IT IS NOT RELYING ON ... (MSCD 3.31).
examples: CUSTOMER MAY NOT RELY ON ANY STATEMENT THAT IS NOT IN THIS AGREEMENT.
LICENSEE MAY NOT REVERSE ENGINEER THE SOFTWARE.
THE LESSEE MAY NOT SUBLET THE EQUIPMENT.
lookalikes: SOME JURISDICTIONS MAY NOT ALLOW THE EXCLUSION OF IMPLIED WARRANTIES.
NEITHER PARTY MAY ASSIGN THIS AGREEMENT WITHOUT THE OTHER PARTY'S CONSENT.

checks.message: Will with a negative subject (Neither party will assign): to prohibit, write Neither party may assign (MSCD 3.111; 3.324; house rule 8). Keep will for policy (Neither party will be liable ...).
examples: Neither party will assign this agreement without the other party's consent.
No Shareholder will transfer any Shares to a Competitor.

If neither party gives notice of nonrenewal, the Term will renew for 1 additional year.
Neither party may assign this agreement without the other party's consent.

checks.message: Will be responsible for: state the duty with shall (Customer shall pay all sales taxes on the Fees) (MSCD 3.111; 3.144). If the point is only that the party bears the liability for a duty owed to a nonparty, such as taxes, Customer is responsible for ... works as language of policy (MSCD 3.145).
examples: Customer will be responsible for paying all sales taxes on the Fees.
Contractor will be responsible for obtaining each permit that the Work requires.
lookalikes: Neither party will be responsible for any delay that a Force Majeure Event causes.
Acme will be solely responsible for the cost of Development.
Customer shall pay all sales taxes on the Fees.

checks.message: Will be required to (or will be obligated to, will have to, will need to) for a duty: write shall (Seller shall indemnify ...) (MSCD 3.111; 3.130).
examples: Seller will be required to indemnify Buyer against any Losses arising out of the Excluded Liabilities.

checks.message: Will not be required to: unless the sentence states the consequence of a contingent future event, write is not required to (Supplier is not required to accept ...) (MSCD 3.296).
examples: Supplier will not be required to accept any Order for fewer than 100 Units.
Licensee will not be required to buy any minimum quantity of Products.
lookalikes: If Customer fails to pay an invoice, Supplier will not be required to accept any further Order.

checks.message: Will have [a period] to: unclear whether it imposes an obligation or states a condition (MSCD 10.94). For a duty, write Seller shall cure the breach no later than 10 Business Days after receiving Buyer's notice; if Buyer's remedy is to depend on a failure to cure, state it as a condition (lawyer's decision).
examples: Seller will have 10 Business Days after receiving Buyer's notice to cure the breach.
Licensee will have until March 1, 2028 to exercise the Option.
lookalikes: Seller shall cure the breach no later than 10 Business Days after receiving Buyer's notice of it.
The Option will have no further effect after March 1, 2028.

checks.message: Will for a party's duty: use shall (MSCD 3.111). Keep will only for future events no party controls.
examples: LICENSEE WILL INDEMNIFY LICENSOR AGAINST ANY CLAIM ARISING OUT OF LICENSEE'S USE OF THE SOFTWARE.
CUSTOMER WON'T REVERSE ENGINEER THE SOFTWARE.
lookalikes: LICENSEE SHALL INDEMNIFY LICENSOR AGAINST ANY CLAIM ARISING OUT OF LICENSEE'S USE OF THE SOFTWARE.
NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT DAMAGES.

checks.message: Must (or must not) for a duty on a party that is the subject: write shall (or shall not) (MSCD 3.107; 3.306). Keep must for a condition (TO EXERCISE THE OPTION, HOLDER MUST ...).
examples: LICENSEE MUST NOT USE THE SOFTWARE TO OPERATE A NUCLEAR FACILITY.
CUSTOMER MUST PAY EACH INVOICE NO LATER THAN 30 DAYS AFTER THE INVOICE DATE.
RESELLER MUST PAY EACH INVOICE NO LATER THAN 30 DAYS AFTER THE INVOICE DATE.
lookalikes: LICENSEE SHALL NOT USE THE SOFTWARE TO OPERATE A NUCLEAR FACILITY.
TO EXERCISE THE OPTION, HOLDER MUST GIVE COMPANY NOTICE.

checks.message: Has to (or needs to) for a duty works like must: write shall (Licensee shall pay ...) (MSCD 3.107; 3.89). For a condition, use must with a to-infinitive (MSCD 3.386).
examples: Licensee has to pay the Royalty on each Unit that Licensee sells.

checks.message: Shouldn't: unclear whether it states a prohibition or advice. For a prohibition write shall not (MSCD 3.89); for advice, recommends that ... not (MSCD 3.502). Don't use contractions in a contract (MSCD 17.37).
examples: Distributor shouldn't sell the Products to a Competitor.
Contractor shouldn’t leave the Site unattended during a concrete pour.

Manufacturer recommends that Distributor not store the Products above 77 degrees Fahrenheit.

checks.message: Knowledge standard (ought to know, constructive knowledge, had reason to know, what a reasonable person would have known): changing the words can change the legal standard, so don't rewrite it. Flag it and offer a defined Knowledge term for Blake's decision: whose knowledge counts, and actual knowledge or knowledge after inquiry (MSCD 13.506; house rule 10).
examples: Contractor shall notify Employer of any Defect of which Contractor knows or ought to know.
Seller states that, to the actual or constructive knowledge of Seller, no Hazardous Material is present on the Property.

checks.message: In the event (without that), in the unlikely event that, in case of: a wordy if. These work like in the event that, which MSCD 17.19 replaces with if: write if (If Buyer terminates ...; if and to the extent that ...).
examples: In the event Buyer terminates this agreement, Seller shall return the Deposit to Buyer.

In case of a conflict between this agreement and a Purchase Order, this agreement will govern.

In each case, Seller shall notify Buyer of the change.
Supplier shall notify Customer of each Force Majeure Event no later than 2 Business Days after it begins.

checks.message: Shall in a conditional or other subordinate clause: use the present tense (If Lender requests ...; If Seller cannot deliver ...) (MSCD 3.358).
examples: Whenever Lender shall so request, Borrower shall give Lender Borrower's most recent financial statements.
In case Seller shall be unable to deliver clear title, Buyer may terminate this agreement.
To the extent that any Loss shall arise out of Seller's negligence, Seller shall indemnify Buyer against it.

checks.message: Shall in a relative clause (each amount that shall become due; the date on which Company shall give notice): shall there marks only future time. Use the present tense (that becomes due; on which Company gives notice) (MSCD 3.507; 3.358). If the clause is meant to impose a duty, state the duty in its own sentence with shall (MSCD 3.89).
examples: Each Share that Investor shall acquire after the date of this agreement is subject to this agreement.

lookalikes: Each Share that Investor owns on the date of this agreement or acquires later is subject to this agreement.
Seller shall ensure that each Unit conforms to the Specifications.

checks.message: Shall (have) in a condition stated as policy: use the present tense or the present perfect (subject to the condition that Buyer has paid ...); with shall, the condition reads as an obligation (MSCD 3.397; 3.395).
examples: Seller's obligation to close is subject to the condition that Buyer shall have paid the Deposit to the Escrow Agent.

examples: Whenever Customer requests, Supplier shall give Customer a report of Supplier's inventory of the Products.
(a) Whenever a Default occurs, Borrower shall notify Lender.

Whenever reasonably practicable, Supplier shall use recycled packaging.

checks.message: When after a duty or discretion: if it introduces a condition, write if (If Customer returns a Unit as defective, Supplier shall give Customer a credit ...) (rider on once and when).
examples: Supplier shall give Customer a credit equal to the Price of a Unit when Customer returns that Unit as defective.
Licensee may terminate this agreement when Licensor fails to deliver an Update.

checks.message: An inverted negative with shall (At no time during the Term shall Tenant ...) works like shall with a negative subject: it reads as an absence of duty, not a prohibition (MSCD 3.324; house rule 8). Write a prohibition: Tenant shall not ... during the Term; for a policy in force now, use the present tense (Licensor is not liable for ...).
examples: At no time during the Term shall Tenant use the Premises for retail sales.

checks.message: Nor shall to continue a prohibition: start a new sentence with language of prohibition (Seller shall not hire ...) (MSCD 3.326).
examples: Seller shall not solicit Buyer's customers, nor shall Seller hire any of Buyer's employees.
Licensee shall not copy the Software, nor will it permit anyone else to do so.
